summary: AE + SE walkthrough of Redwood Console focusing on per-route dashboards, usage analytics, cost breakdown and pilot plan. Customer cares about per-route cost attribution, SLOs by route, and encryption/KMS compliance. Pilot agreed: 2-week test with benchmarking and security review.
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-04-18
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood CSM); Tom Nguyen (Alpine Head of AI), Sara Miller (Platform Eng), Liam O'Connor (CFO), Ben Chu (Security)
transcript: [00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - i'm Jared, AE on the account. priya and maya from our side too. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Tom: Good thanks, Jared. excited to see the console walkthrough. we're trying to understand cost per feature, basically per-route breakdowns.

[00:15] Priya: Awesome. today we'll show the usage analytics, per-route dashboards and the cost breakdowns. we'll also cover caching and recommended pilot setup. quick note: i'll share a benchmark spreadsheet after the call.

[00:30] Sara: one thing up front - we run a mix of chat and single-turn generation, about 2.5M tokens / month today, spiking to 5M on promos. latency SLOs are 300ms p95 for chat. we need to know how Redwood helps with cost/latency tradeoffs.

[00:48] Priya: got it. we'll show how route-level SLOs and per-route batching/caching configs affect costs. also we'll demonstrate the token-level cost breakdown so finance can map spend to product routes.
[01:10] Liam: from finance side i'd like to see allocation by product, not just team. and any automated alerts if cost deviates from forecast.
[01:22] Maya: we have alerting and anomaly detection tied to usage and spend. i'll show the alerts page later and how thresholds map to route usage.
[01:35] Jared: quick qual: are you currently on OpenAI or self-hosted? and any compliance constraints we should know of?

[01:42] Tom: we're on OpenAI right now for prod, but we're evaluating dedicated options. compliance-wise we need SOC 2 and KMS-based encryption, and some data residency controls in the EU for a subset of traffic.
[01:55] Priya: Perfect. Redwood Dedicated and Private options can handle that - we support customer-managed KMS and VPC/private deployments. we'll flag those for the security deep dive.
[02:10] Sara: curious about prefix caching / KV cache - does that work automatically or do we need to modify code?
[02:18] Priya: We have automatic prefix caching for identical prefixes and a KV cache for chat state. for many customers it's zero-code; you can also control eviction TTLs per route in the console.
[02:32] [sound of typing - 02:33] Ben: i want to confirm audit logs - retention and access controls.
[02:38] Maya: audit logs are available, with configurable retention windows. for Private we can integrate with your SIEM. we'll include the audit log spec in the security pack.
[02:50] [03:00] Priya: jumping into the console now - sharing screen. first slide: global usage overview - tokens, requests, error rate. you can filter by model, route, and timeframe.
[03:15] Priya: here is the per-route dashboard. each route has throughput, p50/p95 latency, cost per token, and monthly forecast. see the sidebar where you can tag routes to products.
[03:40] Tom: that forecast looks useful. how accurate is it when traffic is bursty?

[03:47] Priya: forecast uses rolling window and burst factor; we also show a conservative and optimistic estimate. for bursty traffic we suggest enabling burst capacity in Dedicated or a fallback route to a cheaper model.
[04:05] Priya: note the token-level cost breakdown - compute vs infra vs model license. compute is where batching and quantization produce the biggest wins.
[04:18] Sara: can we export per-route CSVs to our internal chargeback system?
[04:22] Jared: yes, CSV export and API access for cost metrics. many finance teams pull that nightly.

[04:30] [04:45] Priya: demonstrating a route-level drilldown - here's 'search-assist' route: average payload size, avg tokens in/out, cache hit rate. you can toggle recommended batching policy; it shows estimated delta in ms and $/1M tokens.
[05:05] Tom: the estimated delta says 22% cost reduction with batching enabled, but p95 goes from 280ms to 320ms. that's in the ballpark we expected.
[05:18] Priya: exactly — tradeoff view. you can pin SLOs per route and automatically apply fallback policies if latency breachs or cost budget exceeded.
[05:30] Liam: curious about how you attribute tokens to a route when user flows call multiple routes for one request?

[05:38] Priya: attribution follows the request context - if your gateway sends route identifiers we map them. if not, we infer from API path. we recommend including route metadata in your calls for accurate chargeback.
[05:55] Sara: we'll definitely include route tags. what's needed from our side to get accurate cost mapping in the pilot?
[06:03] Priya: sample traffic and route tags. Priya: if you can give us 48 hours of representative traffic or a replay file, we can run the dashboard and show concrete numbers.
[06:15] Tom: we can export a 72-hour sample. we'll do that.
[06:20] [06:40] Priya: next, security panel - encryption at rest, KMS integration. for Private we can use customer KMS; for Hosted we support bringing your own key with limited key rotation features.
[06:55] Ben: do you provide attestation for SOC 2?
[06:58] Maya: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II; we'll share the report under NDA. also we provide detailed audit logs and role-based access controls in the console.

[07:10] [07:25] Jared: switching back to cost optimization - Optimize tab recommends quantization profiles per model based on latency targets and token mix. it flags models where 8-bit quantization yields big savings.
[07:40] Tom: do you do any model quality regressions monitoring when quantizing?
[07:45] Priya: yes, Redwood Optimize ties to evals - you can run prompt sets and get quality/regression alerts after changes. we keep the baseline and provide diff reports.
[07:58] Sara: excellent. about dedicated - if we commit to reserved capacity, how granular is the autoscale?
[08:06] Priya: autoscale can be configured by pool with burst capacity. you can set minimum reserved and a burst ceiling, and we support policy-based fallback to hosted if you hit ceiling.
[08:20] Liam: from a contract perspective we'd want a clear SLA and cost predictability; what's typical for pilot-to-prod conversion?
[08:28] Jared: pilots are usually 2 weeks with usage credits. if you convert, we propose a 12-month reserved agreement for Dedicated with an onboarding discount. i'll send an example term sheet.
[08:40] [09:00] Priya: showing alerting - you can create spend alerts per route and trigger webhooks to Slack or PagerDuty. also we have a daily digest e-mail for finance.
[09:12] Tom: one more on multi-region - some EU traffic needs to stay in eu-west-1. can you route by region?
[09:20] Priya: yes, smart routing supports region policies and fallback. we can pin routes to regions or models based on residency rules.
[09:32] Sara: ok, i'm noting items for our infra team - sample traffic export, route tagging, region constraints.
[09:40] [10:05] Ben: on authentication - do you support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning?
[10:10] Maya: yes for enterprise tenants we have SAML and SCIM, RBAC policies in the console, and integration guidelines we'll share.

[10:22] Priya: demo wrap-up - we'll provision a pilot workspace, ingest your sample 72-hour traffic, run a 48-hour benchmark with per-route dashboards and a cost delta report showing batching/caching impact.
[10:40] Tom: sounds good. timeline wise we want results before the exec review on 2026-05-01.
[10:48] Jared: we can aim for that—pilot kickoff next week. i'll send the pricing and pilot agreement today/tomorrow.
[11:00] Sara: quick question on the CSV export format - will it align with our internal chargeback fields?
[11:06] Priya: yes, we can map fields. i'll include a sample CSV schema in the follow-up and coordinate with Sara directly.
[11:16] Liam: please include cost buckets broken down by model, infra, and licensing. CFOs love line items.
[11:24] Jared: noted - full breakdown included. any other questions?
[11:30] Tom: none from me. thanks for the thorough walkthrough.
[11:34] Maya: we'll share the security pack and SOC 2 under NDA, the pricing sheet, and the pilot onboarding doc. expecting Tom to upload sample traffic to the shared drive.

[11:44] Jared: thanks all. next steps recap: Jared send pricing (2026-04-20), Priya sets up pilot & runs benchmark (2026-04-25), Tom uploads traffic (2026-04-22), security deep dive week of 2026-04-27. closing now.
[11:56] Call ended
